correctness.rationale: For each arbitrary mixed binary word, enough zero padding preserves its overlapping occurrence count. Bitwise reflection sends it to the complemented word, with exactly one possible added leading-zero boundary occurrence depending only on the complemented pattern. Every finite common-step progression therefore reverses to a common-step progression of the complementary pattern with uniformly shifted parity, and the converse follows by exchanging patterns. This proves equality of suprema for any d; exact checker passed 229710 configurations. Finite tests do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: This universally answers an explicit natural published question for all mixed binary patterns and every positive progression difference. The exact reversal statement is structurally stronger than maximal-run equality, identifies the only boundary term induced by conventional leading zeros, and applies to all finite arithmetic-progression color words. The distinction from constant patterns and from progressions forced to start at zero is mathematically substantive.
